Mediate

MEE-dee-ayt -- three syllables, stress on the first syllable, MEE. Don't confuse it with 'meditate,' which has a T and means to reflect quietly. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To mediate intervene between two parties.

The city hired a professional to mediate between the developers and the neighborhood association.

Worked Example

Two roommates haven't spoken in a week over the mess in the kitchen, so a third friend sits them both down, hears each side, and helps them write a chore schedule they can both accept.

That friend mediated the dispute -- stepped in between the two sides as a neutral helper and guided them to their own agreement. To mediate is to intervene between parties in conflict, never to take a side.

How Mediate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

arbitrate

arbitrate: hear both sides of a dispute and decide it for them

intercede

intercede: step in on someone's behalf

reconcile

reconcile: bring people back into friendly relations

Antonyms

inflame

inflame: make a conflict worse

divide

divide: drive people apart

How Strong Is It? — arbitrate → mediate → intercede

arbitrate vs. mediate

arbitrate vs. mediate: Arbitrate carries more power than mediate: a mediator stands between two sides and helps them find their own agreement, while an arbitrator listens and then hands down a decision they must accept.

intercede vs. mediate

intercede vs. mediate: Intercede leans to one side, while mediate stays in the middle -- you intercede for your friend with the angry coach, but you mediate between two friends who are angry at each other.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — medi-

root — medi-: middle (Latin medius)

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: to make, to act (Latin -atus)

Put it together

Put it together: Mediate is built on Latin medius, 'middle,' plus the verb ending -ate: 'to be in the middle.' A mediator plants themselves squarely between two quarreling parties -- in the middle, belonging to neither side.

Use the root in a new word: intermediate

Use the root in a new word: intermediate: She enrolled in the intermediate swim class, halfway between beginner and advanced.

Root Check

Word Choice

Mediate takes a dispute as its object or brings 'between' along: mediate a conflict, mediate between labor and management. The mediator must be neutral -- if you take a side, you are advocating, not mediating. And mind the spelling: meditate, with a T, means to reflect quietly alone.
